results.title: DSAssassin: Cross-VM Side-Channel Attacks by Exploiting Intel Data Streaming Accelerator (HPCA 2026)
results.summary: HPCA 2026 paper demonstrating that Intel DSA, a user-programmable high-throughput data mover for memcpy/memset/checksum offload on Sapphire Rapids-and-later Xeons, can be abused as a cross-VM side channel via its shared work queue. Directly characterizes DSA's data-movement microarchitecture.

results.title: DSAssassin Artifact (HPCA '26 reproduction repository)
results.summary: Primary artifact repository for the HPCA '26 DSAssassin paper, containing reverse-engineering experiments and attack/evaluation code against Intel DSA on Ubuntu 24.04 with DSA-equipped Xeon hardware. MIT-licensed research artifact.

results.title: A Quantitative Analysis and Guidelines of Data Streaming Accelerator in Modern Intel Xeon Scalable Processors (ASPLOS'24)
results.summary: Comprehensive evaluation of Intel DSA as a high-performance data copy and transformation accelerator introduced in Sapphire Rapids, covering data-movement operations, CRC32/DIF/delta-record offload, and a DPDK Vhost case study with programmer guidelines. CC BY 4.0.

results.title: intel/idxd-config (accel-config / libaccel-config)
results.summary: Official Intel utility library for configuring the DSA (Data Streaming Accelerator) and IAA (In-Memory Analytics Accelerator) subsystems in the Linux kernel via the idxd driver; the primary tool (accel-config) used to enable memcpy/data-movement offload engines.

results.title: Accelerating Memory-Bandwidth-Bound Kernels Using Intel DSA
results.summary: Intel official technical article describing how to combine DSA offload with CPU execution to accelerate memory-bandwidth-bound data-movement kernels using fewer cores.

results.title: Intel Begins Preparing Linux For Next-Gen DSA 3.0 Accelerators
results.summary: Covers Intel's June 2025 Linux kernel patch series exposing next-generation DSA 3.0 capability registers in the IDXD driver, discussing the DSA block's role in offloading data movement from CPU cores and a possible Diamond Rapids debut.
